title: Two Hamzahs in One Word - when the second carries a dhamma: أَ اُ
titleEn: Two Hamzahs in One Word - when the second carries a dhamma: أَ اُ
description: Refer to the `two hamzahs in one word - when both carry hamzahs carry a fatha` for an introduction to these rules. There are a total of 3 places in the quran where the pre-requisites for this rule, i.e. two Hamzahs in one Word with the second carrying a dhamma, occur.

tashil_of_second_with_idkhal.title: Tashῑl of 2nd with idkhāl
tashil_of_second_with_idkhal.description: Tashῑl of 2nd with idkhāl means to recite the first of the two hamzahs clearly (taḥqīq), inserting an alif after it thereby creating a natural madd and reciting the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel wāw.
exceptions: Imam Hisham only applies this option in 2 places. These are: أَؤُنْزِلَ and أَؤُلْقِيَ (occuring at 38:8 and 54:25 respectively)
tashil_of_second_with_idkhal.note: This is one of two options for Imam Abu 'Amr.

tashil_of_second_without_idkhal.title: Tashῑl of 2nd without idkhāl
tashil_of_second_without_idkhal.description: Tashῑl of 2nd without idkhāl means to recite the first of the two hamzahs clearly (taḥqīq) and reciting the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel wāw.
tashil_of_second_without_idkhal.note: This is one of two options for Imam Abu 'Amr

tahqiq_of_both_with_idkhal.title: Taḥqīq of both with idkhāl
tahqiq_of_both_with_idkhal.description: Both hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) and the first will be elongated as an alif of madd in inserted after it (idkhāl).

tahqiq_of_both_without_idkhal.title: Taḥqīq of both without idkhāl
tahqiq_of_both_without_idkhal.description: Both hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) with no changes made to either.
